chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: My mother gave me her share in the house as charity. So I said to her: The judges do not approve this, but write it as a sale. She said: Do from that whatever appears suitable to you, and everything that you see to be permissible for you. So I secured it, and then some of the heirs wanted to make me swear that I had paid her the price, while I had not paid her anything. So what do you think?
He عليه السلام said: “Then swear to them.”

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: The sale price or payment amount.
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَتْ: She gave as charity or donation.
key_terms.شِرًى: A sale transaction or purchase form.
key_terms.فَاحْلِفْ: So swear; an instruction to take the oath.
key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفَنِي: They seek to make me swear an oath.

ai.seo_question: Can a person swear regarding a documented property transfer challenged by heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal dispute involving a mother's transfer of her share in a house to her son and the later challenge raised by other heirs. The Imam عليه السلام permits the son to swear in support of the documented form of the transaction, indicating a ruling related to oaths and disputed property arrangements.
